reason: The crank and ratchet wheel appear to belong on the winding drum, which will wind the lifting cord.
expectation: They should form a hand-operated winding mechanism.

effect: The drum and crank form a hand winch, ready to be fitted to the crane.
reaction: The trade-off between crank length and hand travel is interesting.
reason: The crane needs the winch to wind its lifting cord.
expectation: The winch should attach to the crane frame.

effect: The winch is now attached to the crane, so the lifting cord can be fitted next.
reaction: That was a straightforward assembly step.
reason: The cord and hook need to connect the winch to a load, presumably passing over the tip pulley.
expectation: The cord and hook should be fitted to the crane’s lifting mechanism.

effect: The crane now has its lifting line; it still needs a way to hold a load and a safe test.
reaction: The assembly is progressing as expected.
reason: The holding pawl should engage the ratchet so the winch can hold a raised load.
expectation: The pawl and release lever should fit to the winch and provide a controlled hold and release.

effect: The pawl can hold the drum, but the crane still needs protection against tipping.
reaction: The distinction between holding the rope and stabilizing the whole crane is useful.
reason: The rear ballast block should help balance the crane before testing a load.
expectation: The ballast should attach at the rear and make the crane more stable.

effect: The ballast cannot currently be combined with anything, so I’ll test the rigged crane first.
reaction: That was unexpected; I thought ballast would be fitted before testing.
reason: The padded test weight offers a cautious way to check the lifting mechanism before using the basket.
expectation: The crane should attempt to lift and hold the test weight, revealing whether it is stable.

effect: The low test showed that the pawl holds the rope but the crane tips, so rear ballast is now needed.
reaction: The test made the difference between holding and balancing concrete.
reason: The rear ballast should counter the load that lifted the rear feet.
expectation: The ballast should stabilize the crane for another test.

effect: The ballast keeps all the feet down during the low test, and the pawl holds the drum until the release is eased.
reaction: The separate jobs of ballast and pawl are clearer now.
reason: The crane has passed the low test, so the cargo basket is the remaining load to try.
expectation: The crane should lift, hold and gently lower the basket.

effect: The basket test completed the goal: the pawl held it aloft, and controlling the crank and release lowered it gently.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the tested mechanisms work together on the basket.

mostWorthwhile.text: The low test and ballast correction made the difference between holding a load and preventing a crane from tipping clear. That practical distinction felt worth the time.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial winch assembly and fitting were straightforward but less revealing than the later tests.

surprise.text: I expected to fit the ballast before testing, but it was unavailable until the crane began to tip in the supported low test.

arbitrary.text: Making the ballast unavailable before the test felt somewhat arbitrary, even though the subsequent demonstration explained why it was needed.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the crane's test and correction gave the construction a useful purpose beyond simply fitting parts together.
